python3 -c "
import cv2
import numpy as np

img = cv2.imread('/work/observations/obs_0062.png')
# Cabinet top is light grey/white
# Let's inspect RGB values across horizontal line y=400, y=450, y=350
print('Row 440:', img[440, 200:300:20])
print('Row 350:', img[350, 200:300:20])

# Find cabinet mask: white top, light wood side
# top face is very light grey/white: R~230+, G~230+, B~230+
# front face: white R~255, G~255, B~255
# right side: light wood/tan R~210-230, G~190-210, B~160-180
mask_front = (img[:, :, 0] > 240) & (img[:, :, 1] > 240) & (img[:, :, 2] > 240)
ys, xs = np.where(mask_front)
print(f'Front face x: [{xs.min()}, {xs.max()}], y: [{ys.min()}, {ys.max()}]')

# Bottom of the front face:
# Let's find the bottommost row of the white cabinet front
print('Front face bottom row:', ys.max())
print('Front face left x:', xs[ys == ys.max()].min(), 'right x:', xs[ys == ys.max()].max())

# Top face back edge:
mask_top = (img[:, :, 0] > 200) & (img[:, :, 0] < 240) & (img[:, :, 1] > 200) & (img[:, :, 1] < 240) & (img[:, :, 2] > 200) & (img[:, :, 2] < 240)
# Let's check bounding box of top
ys_t, xs_t = np.where(mask_top)
if len(ys_t) > 0:
    print(f'Top face x: [{xs_t.min()}, {xs_t.max()}], y: [{ys_t.min()}, {ys_t.max()}]')
"
